page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.c7nex.large is an entry-tier x86_64 server instance within the enhanced ecs.c7nex family. Powered by a 2.7 GHz Intel Xeon 8369B processor, it features 1 physical core with hyperthreading enabled to provide 2 dedicated vCPUs. System memory is configured at 4.0 GB, yielding a 1:2 vCPU-to-RAM ratio of 2.0 GB per thread. The instance includes no local NVMe or SSD storage and relies entirely on external network-attached volumes. Network connectivity is capped at a 3 Gbps baseline bandwidth.

Benchmark evaluations highlight a notable distinction between single-threaded and multi-threaded capabilities. Single-core performance is aligned with general industry averages, as demonstrated by a stress-ng single-core score of 1847.58, a Geekbench single-core score of 1500.0, and single-threaded gzip compression at 27.77 GB/sec. Conversely, multi-core metrics fall into lower benchmark percentiles due to the underlying single physical core architecture, recorded in stress-ng multi-core (1930.87), Geekbench multi-core (1751.0), and PassMark CPU (2950.81). Uncached memory read and write throughput testing yielded 14.01 GB/sec and 12.76 GB/sec respectively.

The hardware configuration offers a low-overhead platform for execution profiles that depend on steady single-threaded core performance rather than parallel scaling. Resource limitations in memory bandwidth and multi-core processing constrain suitability for heavy compiled applications, complex database instances, or high-throughput analytics. Best-fit deployments include lightweight web serving, low-concurrency API microservices, text processing pipelines, and simple single-threaded background execution jobs.

Benchmark evaluations place its single-core CPU execution and single-threaded decompression within average performance bands, whereas multi-core benchmarks, memory read/write bandwidth, and database operations fall into lower performance tiers due to the single-core constraint. With a 1:2 RAM-to-vCPU ratio, ecs.c7nex.large provides a low-overhead platform for low-concurrency execution profiles, light web serving, basic microservices, and single-threaded utility tasks that do not demand extensive memory throughput or parallel processing.
